extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, IP practitioners, in-house counsel, and patent applicants with interest in Thailand
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of proposed amendments to Thailand's Patent Act and related design-patent/legal-procedural changes, including substantive patentability standards, prosecution timelines, compulsory licenses, PCT provisions, and fees. Useful for practitioners advising clients or preparing filings in Thailand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of genetic resources, genetic material, derivative works, and traditional knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3 requires disclosure of the source of genetic resources (GRs), genetic materials, derivative works, and traditional knowledge (TK) used for development of the claimed inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents and agreements relating to access and benefit-sharing must be submitted along with applications for patent registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worldwide novelty (state of the art includes outside the country)
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'outside the country' is added to 'state of the art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventions widely known or used either within or outside Thailand will not be patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of double patenting (Thai prior art effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a patent filed in Thailand, even if it is published on or after the date of a later-filed application in Thailand, will be considered state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This makes explicit that earlier-filed Thai applications can defeat later-filed applications (addresses double-patenting concerns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period for disclosure prior to filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures of the subject matter of an invention made no more than 12 months before filing will not be taken into account in two instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two instances are: (1) a disclosure occasioned by the subject matter having been obtained unlawfully; and (2) a disclosure made by the inventor, the applicant, or their authorized representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patentability of surgical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Surgical methods considered methods of treatment are added to the list of non-patentable subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods of treatment (including surgical methods) will be excluded from patentable subject matter under the draft amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual publication and opposition procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications will be published twice—first within 18 months of the application’s filing date in Thailand, and again after substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opposition period is 90 days from the second publication date; if there has been no opposition by the end of that period the patent will be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request separation (division) of a patent application before the second publication of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the current Act such a request is not allowed and separation can only be done at the examiner's discretion; the draft permits applicant-requested division prior to second publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for requesting substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The period for requesting substantive examination is reduced to three years from the application’s filing date in Thailand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces the present five years from the publication date, shortening the available window to request substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation of license agreements (formality only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement changed from registration of a patent license agreement to recordation of a license agreement with the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only a formality examination will be conducted on recorded license agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error correction in granted patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits correction of trivial errors found in a patent after it has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections are allowed provided they do not expand the scope of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annuity non-payment, abandonment, and surcharge
rubrics_metrics.description: Director-general may designate a patent abandoned if its annuity fee is not paid by the due date, but the Board of Patents may revoke the director-general’s order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon receiving a revocation petition, the Board may grant an extension to pay the annuity fee subject to a 50% surcharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licenses for medicines (import and export)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes ministries, sub-ministries, and government departments to issue compulsory licenses to import patented medicines for public use, in line with Article 31 bis of the TRIPS Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also provides for issuance of compulsory licenses to export medicines to countries with insufficient or no pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: New PCT-related chapter
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds a chapter for international applications under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers applicant qualifications, filing procedures, priority claims, restoration of priority rights, and related PCT issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination request for petty patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The period for requesting substantive examination of a petty patent is changed to six years (increased from one year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for substantive examination can be filed at any time by any person, regardless of their interest in the petty patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of design patent examination (before publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of design patent applications will be moved to occur prior to publication of the design patent application in Thailand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After examination the DIP will publish the design application and accept oppositions for up to 90 days from the publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of design publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Deferral of publication of a design patent application can be requested in compliance with rules and procedures specified in the DIP director-general’s guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regardless of any deferral request, the DIP may proceed with examination or issuance of office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period for responding to design office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadline for responding to an office action will be shortened from 90 days to 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant can request a one-time extension for another 60 days (i.e., one 60-day extension available).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial design protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows protection of partial designs; the definition of 'designs' includes 'part of an article that is visible to the naked eye.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial features of an article that are visible can be claimed and protected as design patents under the draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related design (principal design) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'principal design' allows protection of related designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related design applications must have the same title and applicant, bear similarity to the principal design, be filed within six months of the principal design's filing date, and protection for the related design starts from the filing date of the principal design. An assignor can assign related designs together as a set to one assignee for the same period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of design patent protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patent protection allowed for 15 years including all possible renewals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consists of five years after registration/grant plus two renewals of five years each (5 + 5 + 5 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Late renewal payment for design patents
rubrics_metrics.description: For a renewal filed more than six months after the expiration date, the patent owner must request that the director-general allow late payment of the renewal fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late renewal will incur a surcharge of 50 percent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of patent design rights and examples of non-infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent design owner's rights are applicable only within the boundaries of the drawings, title, claims, and brief description of the design patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material/properties/utilization/benefits from features not within the rights are not allowed to be exploited. Examples listed as non-infringement include: private use with no commercial interest; research and experiments that do not conflict with owner’s benefits; prior use in good faith; temporary/emergency entry by equipment of ship vessels; and use after receiving consent from the owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hague Agreement accession: filing and applicant requirements for designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon accession to the Hague Agreement, DIP will receive international applications designating Thailand; applicants must have Thai nationality or be Thai-registered juristic persons with residence or real industrial/commercial activities in Thailand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International applications designating Thailand are considered filed in Thailand with the WIPO registration date as the Thai filing date. Because Thailand currently accepts only single-design applications, WIPO multiple-design applications will be rejected and must be amended or separated into single-design filings. The designation fee for Thailand will be at standard designation fee level three, and the DIP will examine novelty and other substantive grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government fees for design patent filings, extensions, and renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: Government filing fee increased to THB 3,000 (approx. USD 100) and will include filing, publication, and registration fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee for requesting an extension of time is THB 5,000 (approx. USD 660). Design renewal fees are payable for five-year periods (replacing annual payments) and will be THB 20,000 for the first renewal and THB 49,000 for the second renewal (approx. USD 660 and USD 1,620 respectively).
